title: Duke Heinrich the Younger with his councillors on Brunswick and Goslar, the Rammelsberg and the libel against Saxony and Hesse: large parts in cipher
correspondents: Heinrich the Younger of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel ↔ his councillors
status: Finding aid as quoted. Not digitised. A printed study (https://www.sav.sk/journals/uploads/0307161001500opt.pdf, search snippet only) reproduces a single-letter cipher of Heinrich c. 1540 from 1 Alt 8 Nr. 490, so this may be a key lookup; not promoted.
why: The feud with the Schmalkaldic League that cost Heinrich his duchy in 1542.
score_note: Scored from the finding-aid description during the Nov 2026 German portals sweep 2 (research/sweep_2026-11_german_portals_2/); not viewed
verify: Blocked (review 3 Nov 2026): 1 Alt 8 Nr. 549 (1540-42, 'Große Teile chiffriert') is not digitised. Strasser 2017 (read in full) prints Heinrich's own key from 1 Alt 8 as Fig. 3, c. 1540: signs with homophones, 'Duplices', 'Errantes' and names including the Landgrave of Hesse and the Schmalkaldic League, plus a ciphered letter from Nr. 490 f. 36r as Fig. 12. Same duke, fonds and years, so a key lookup is likely but untested. Blocker: a scan, to try Fig. 3. Catalogue 1971's key_check predates this and says no key is held; it should cite Strasser.

correspondents: Samuel Wharton → Edward Bancroft; → John Williams

status: Finding aid: "(In cipher.)". Papers of Franklin says of Wharton's 1777 code letter to Bancroft that the editors could not identify the people behind the code numbers.
